sentences.text: (Lodged In Sub Jail Balotra)
----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Deepak Menaria
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Pawan Kumar Bhati, PP  Mr. Rajendra Beniwal  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 08/01/2025
The petitioner has been arrested in connection with FIR No. 135/2022 registered at Police Station, Siwana, District Barmer for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B IPC.
He has preferred this second bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that after rejection of first bail application, statement of material witnesses have been recorded including the brother of the deceased.
The father of deceased Om Prakash has been examined in Court as PW/1, brother Govind Ram has been examined as PW/7 and there are material contradictions in the statement of these witnesses.
The doctor who conducted the postmortem has been examined as PW/ 16 and he has categorically stated that there were no visible injuries on the person of deceased.

It is argued that the petitioner [2025:RJ-JD:1161] (2 of 2)
[CRLMB-2217/2024] was arrested on 16.03.2023 and is behind the bars for almost two yaers,
therefore, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application and submits that all the witnesses have specifically named the present petitioner.

Moreover, eighteen prosecution witnesses have already been examined and trial is at the fag end, therefore, the present case is not a fit case for extending bail to the accused petitioner at this stage.

sentences.text: I have considered the arguments advanced before me and carefully gone through the record.
The first bail application filed by the petitioner was dismissed as not pressed vide order dated 04.09.2023.
The petitioner is the husband of deceased and as per statement of witnesses, there is specific allegation with regard to demand of dowry and harassment meted out to the deceased.
The death of wife was caused within a short span of marriage in her matrimonial home.

Moreover,
eighteen witnesses have already been examined and trial is at the fag end.
The petitioner being the principal accused, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of bail to the petitioner.
The present second bail application having no merit, is hereby dismissed.
However, trial court is directed to expedite the trial.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 94-BJSH/-
